# Gelabber v0.9.3

Integrated through #499 to #506 and #508 into `v0.9` and the version PR into
`main`.

Fixes from a review of the whole codebase at v0.9.2: security fixes in the
desktop app, the server and the deployment, a push-to-talk that closes the
microphone, calls that survive a short server hiccup, and many smaller bugs
in both clients. There is one database migration (`0029`, two indexes).
`compose.yaml` changes in its image pins, in coturn's start and in the API
settings it passes on; `.env` gains one optional setting.

**Update soon.** Several fixes close security holes that are in v0.9.2.

## Security

- **Desktop: links open without a shell (#505).** A link in a message was
  handed to `cmd /C start` on Windows, so a crafted link could run a
  command. Links now go through one opener that takes only `http`, `https`
  and `mailto` and hands them to the system directly.
- **Desktop: TLS for the gateway and media sockets is checked against the
  system's trust store, and the session stays off foreign origins (#504).**
  Downloads are capped by kind; the session cookie is dropped at sign-out.
- **coturn no longer relays to private addresses (#499).** A member with
  TURN credentials could reach services inside the Compose network through
  the relay. coturn now relays over UDP only and refuses private, loopback
  and link-local peers. See the upgrade notes for
  `TURN_ALLOWED_PEER_IPS`.
- **Deleted and edited messages leave the replay log (#500).** The gateway
  kept the old text for clients that resume; an edit or delete now rewrites
  the message's entries.
- **Sign-in and hashing are bounded (#501).** A password guess is counted
  before Argon2 runs, at most one hash runs per core, and CSRF is checked
  before a request is counted. Mail has separate budgets, ten an hour per
  inbox.
- **Access is checked again under the server lock (#501).** Send, edit,
  delete and preview removal recheck a member who was kicked or banned in
  the same moment. A ban deletes the banned member's invites.
- **Downloads sign their response headers; the metrics label, the
  post-login redirect and one account's sockets are bounded (#500, #501,
  #502).** At most 16 sockets per account, and one 5 s deadline per
  subscribe replay.
- **Image builds no longer trust any presented crates.io chain (#499).**
  See the upgrade notes.

## Calls

- **Push-to-talk closes the microphone on the desktop (#504, #505).**
  Resuming the producer re-enabled the track, so the microphone stayed open
  with the key up. The gate now sits on the track. The key is recorded and
  matched by its place on the keyboard, so Z and Y are right on a German
  layout. The window lets the key go when it is hidden, loses focus, or the
  microphone fails; it holds only from a press it has seen.
- **Holding the push-to-talk key no longer hangs the window (#505).**
- **A short server problem no longer ends the call (#500, #503, #504).**
  The media server answers `gone` when it could not check access (Redis
  error, lost worker) and `unauthorized` only for a real no. Both clients
  rebuild the seat with a new ticket. The fourth unasked revocation within
  a minute ends the call with a message.
- **The camera no longer streams while the app shows it off (#504).** A
  camera switch that fails turns the camera off on the desktop.
- A plugged-in microphone and a new system default are picked up in the
  web client (#503). A kick or ban ends the call on the desktop (#504).
- The media server takes at most 8 peers per user and 256 per room (#500).

## Server

- Live presence reaches DMs; a channel delete touches only its own
  sockets; shutdown closes sockets with 1012 and refuses upgrades while it
  drains; push is held back only for a page in front that follows the
  channel (#500).
- An image past 16384 px on a side or 64 megapixels is refused. Proxy
  uploads end on an idle body instead of at 60 s. Stored link-preview
  images count against the author's quota (#501).
- Registration takes only bare addresses and stores the ASCII form of the
  domain. Kick, ban and server delete wait at most 5 s for the server row
  and then answer `rate_limited` (#501).
- An unclosed `<@` no longer swallows the mention after it; search refuses
  control characters (#501).

## Web

- The composer's emoji and GIF pickers no longer submit the form; an open
  message edit survives scrolling; dialogs close only on a press and
  release on the backdrop; only a modal dialog blocks Strg+F and Esc
  (#503).
- A failed password change, or one running in another tab, keeps the
  account. A silent socket is dropped without waiting for its close. Theme
  sync no longer sticks after a lost write (#502).
- A page that throws shows a German error with "Neu laden". The sign-in
  artwork is a 123 KB WebP (#502).
- An image too large in pixels says so, and registration refuses the
  address forms the server will not store (#506).

## Desktop

- **A very large picture no longer crashes the app (#505).** Pictures are
  scaled to the device and kept in a 256 MB budget; one over 50 megapixels
  is shown as a download link.
- "Weitere Themes" no longer freezes the settings (#505).
- Attachments are saved through a file dialog and attached off the UI
  thread; drafts, dialogs and search hits belong to the signed-in account;
  leaving a server does not lead back into it (#505).
- The client retries a failed recovery, keeps deleted messages out of
  older pages, and writes a log file and panics to the config directory
  (#504).
- A failed "sign out everywhere" says the other devices are not signed out
  and retries as such (#506).
- An unreadable `native-state.json` is moved aside instead of overwritten.
  Per-person volumes move once into `user-volumes.json` (#505).

## Upgrade notes

- The image pins `GELABBER_{API,WEB,MEDIA}_IMAGE` move together to
  `v0.9.3`. Update the server and the desktop apps together: a 0.9.2
  desktop app does not know the new `gone` answer.
- **Migration `0029`** adds two indexes and changes no data. It runs at the
  API's start.
- **coturn:** if your SFU is reached through TURN on a private address,
  set `TURN_ALLOWED_PEER_IPS` (IPv4 addresses or CIDR ranges) in `.env`, or
  relayed calls fail. A literal address in `MEDIA_ADVERTISED_IP` is allowed
  by itself; a hostname there is skipped with a warning.
- **Building images behind a TLS-inspecting proxy** now stops with a
  message. Pass `--build-arg TRUST_PRESENTED_CRATES_CA=true` to trust the
  chain the proxy presents.
- **Before the upgrade** you can run
  `SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE email ~ '[^[:ascii:]]'`. If it is 0, no
  account has an address with a non-ASCII domain, and nothing needs
  attention. Otherwise such an account keeps its spelling, and the same
  address could be registered once more in its ASCII form.
- **Push-to-talk on a German keyboard:** record the key once more in the
  settings to get the corrected global binding.
- **Rollback, server:** the v0.9.2 image set plus the database backup from
  before the upgrade. v0.9.2 does not start on a database that has
  migration `0029`.
- **Desktop, Windows:** the native app offers the update itself.
- **Desktop, Linux (Arch):** `pacman -Syu`.

## CI

- The deploy job also runs the deployment tools' tests, changed areas
  count a move's source, a hand-started pre-release is never Latest, and
  only a version release starts the desktop release build (#499).
- The install tests' import check reads per-person volumes from
  `user-volumes.json`, where the app keeps them since #505 (#508).

## Open

- Nothing was tried in a real browser, the running desktop app, a real
  call or a live stack. The checks are the test suites, CI's loopback call
  and a Windows type-check; the Windows-only code (link opener, file
  dialogs, single instance) has not been run by hand.
- The new limits (sockets, peers, pixels, mails, the 5 s waits) were
  chosen, not measured. Every message write now takes a share lock on its
  server row; on a very busy channel a ban could hit the 5 s wait.
- Not in this release, each needs a decision: binding SFU access to a voice
  seat (a member can still listen without appearing in the roster), a
  switch to close registration, proxying link avatars, a Redis password in
  Compose, a protocol version handshake.
- Mouse 4/5 as the push-to-talk key reads the button state, and the Linux
  portal is offered a US key for punctuation and dead keys.
